text: Why does the single ESN struggle on the multi-timescale envelope task while the DeepESN succeeds?
choices: A single reservoir has one characteristic effective timescale, so it cannot simultaneously track the fast oscillation and the slow envelope; the stacked layers supply multiple timescales
The single ESN cannot be trained by ridge regression, whereas the deep stack can
The deep ESN has far more reservoir neurons (3000 vs 300) than the single ESN
The single ESN violates the echo state property, while the deep ESN satisfies it
explanation: A shallow reservoir shares one effective time constant across all neurons, forcing a compromise between tracking the 50 Hz carrier and the 5 Hz envelope; the deep stack of decreasing-α layers separates the timescales. Both models use ridge regression (option 1 false) and both satisfy the ESP (option 3 false). Crucially, the deep net does NOT have more neurons: 3×100 = 300 = N_SINGLE (option 2 false); the gain is from depth/timescales, not size.
